We also thank the staff at the Italian National Supercomputing Centre (CINECA) for providing HPC facilities under the initiative for specific scientific applications. Finally, we are indebted to the Dark Energy Survey (DES) for making their data accessible. This project received partial funding from the Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research (MIUR) and the European Union's Horizon 2020 research and innovation program under grant agreement No 871124. The authors declare no conflicts of interest.

This study introduces a novel framework for cross-language sentiment analysis (CLSA) that requires no parallel training data. The approach leverages multiple NLP tasks to enable zero-shot CLSA, utilizing a multi-task learning (MTL) architecture. Specifically, the model employs a shared bottom layer to extract semantic features from both source and target languages, while distinct top layers handle sentiment classification in the source language, cross-lingual sentiment prediction, and classification in the target language. Extensive experiments were conducted on three datasets: Chinese-English, Chinese-French, and Chinese-German. Results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches. Furthermore, the framework is adaptable to various language pairs and can be extended to additional tasks, such as predicting sentiment in under-resourced languages. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/Abhishek-1999/MTL-CLSA.

We present evidence that the surface angular velocity of the neutron star in the low-mass X-ray binary 4U 1608-52 has recently accelerated by a factor of two, reaching a value of $\Omega_{\rm K}$ at the inner stable orbit. This acceleration occurred without the creation of a type-I instability strip, implying that the angular velocity of the accretion disk at the neutron star's surface has also recently surpassed $\Omega_{\rm K}$ at the inner stable orbit. These findings challenge the standard model of angular momentum transport in accretion disks, which predicts that the surface angular velocity remains below $\Omega_{\rm R}$ at the inner edge. We propose two potential explanations for this anomaly: either the neutron star has recently consumed a low-mass planet orbiting near the inner stable orbit, or a new mechanism for angular momentum transport has become active at the corresponding radius. If the planetary consumption model is correct, this event offers a method for detecting and identifying planets within the inner regions of extrasolar systems. Furthermore, if the surface angular velocity can exceed $\Omega_{\rm R}$ at the inner edge, the maximum mass-shedding limit for neutron star accretion disks may be significantly higher than currently assumed, potentially allowing disks to sustain higher viscous stresses and enabling the growth of low-mass neutron star binaries from initially wider configurations. Ultimately, the recent spin-up of 4U 1608-52 provides a compelling case study for investigating the physical processes governing angular momentum transport in astrophysical accretion disks. The observations supporting this report are drawn from the RXTE/PCA, ASCA, XMM-Newton, and Chandra X-ray satellites, complemented by optical data from the TESS satellite and the Palomar Transient Factory. Additional details regarding the binary's orbital parameters were derived using timing data collected by the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope.

Fake news spreads rapidly across social media, posing significant challenges for human verification. While deep learning models have been effective at identifying false content from verified articles, their application to unseen articles remains limited due to data scarcity. Although neural process networks (NPN) offer a promising direction for handling out-of distribution data, they have not yet been successfully applied to the task of detecting false news from unverified texts. This study introduces a meta learning-based approach designed to identify fake news in unseen articles using both textual and visual information. We propose Meta FNet, a novel architecture that integrates an embedding layer, a meta task classifier, and an NPN classifier. Extensive experiments conducted on two real-world datasets demonstrate that Meta FNet effectively detects fake news in unseen articles and outperforms current state-of-the-art methods. The source code is available at: https://github.com/Abhishek-1999/MultiModalEmergentFalseNewsDetectionviaMetaNeuralProcessNetworks.

Golay complementary arrays (GCAs) represent a significant advancement over Golay complementary sequences (GCS) and Golay complementary matrices (GCMs), offering superior autocorrelation properties. This paper introduces two novel constructions of GCA pairs with lengths $N_1 N_2 + N_1 + N_2$ and $N_1 N_2 - N_1 - N_2$ across arbitrary $p$-tuples of polyphase domains. These constructions are demonstrated to be optimal within their respective lengths. Furthermore, the concept of concatenated GCAs is generalized to a $p$-fold hierarchy, termed $p$-fold Golay complementary arrays (p-GCA). Utilizing the newly defined GCA pairs and the $p$-fold GCA framework, two distinct designs of GCA pairs in a 3-fold polyphase environment are presented. Finally, a concrete example illustrating the construction of a 4-fold GCA pair is provided. The proposed designs of Golay complementary $p$-tuples are applicable to radar systems, wireless communications, and optical imaging. These constructions are detailed in the appendix of the corresponding manuscript titled: "Designs of Golay Complementary Arrays in a Polyphase Environment and Their Applications" by Y. Wang, X. Li, and Y. Zhang, published in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, Volume 67, Issue 11. The DOI for that manuscript is 10.1109/TIT.2021.3093760.

Synthetic data serves as a crucial resource for training deep learning models, particularly in medical domains where acquiring real data is difficult. While Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated success in specific tasks, they often struggle with training instability and an inability to generate diverse samples. Variational Auto-Encoders (VAEs) offer a more stable alternative but typically produce lower fidelity outputs. To address these limitations, we introduce the Brain Injury Synthesis Progressive Adversarial Variational Auto-Encoder (BISPVAE). This framework combines a VAE with a progressive GAN to enhance the fidelity of generated images. Leveraging the hierarchical characteristics of brain injury data, BISPVAE employs a multi-stage approach: initially, a Variational Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (VC-GAN) upsamples low-resolution CT scans to an intermediate resolution, followed by the main BISPVAE model processing these images to a final resolution. Extensive experiments on a real-world brain injury dataset demonstrate that BISPVAE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both fidelity and diversity. Furthermore, the synthetic data created using our framework effectively supports the training of brain injury detection models. Our code and dataset are accessible at https://github.com/BrainInjurySynthesis/BISPVAE.

Feature extraction via contrastive learning has gained traction in computer vision, particularly for tasks like zero-shot and few-shot learning where models are trained on massive image datasets without specific annotations. Despite its growing popularity, the field lacks a unified framework that integrates various contrastive learning strategies. This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for contrasting image features, encompassing three distinct approaches: instance, pair, and triplet-based learning. We demonstrate that instance-based and pair-based methods are mathematically equivalent, while triplet-based learning can be expressed as a linear combination of these two. To validate this unified framework, we applied it to three specific feature extraction methods: Barlow Twins, InfoNCE, and Triplet Loss. Our experiments show that these methods, when used with a ResNet-50 backbone, achieve state-of-the-art results across multiple zero-shot and few-shot learning benchmarks. Furthermore, we conducted an analysis of feature space quality using t-SNE and evaluated performance under different batch sizes. The source code is available at: https://github.com/AbdulrahmanAlshammari/UnifiedContrastiveLearning.

Although large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable success, their performance is constrained by the volume of training data and the inherent biases present within it. To address these limitations, we introduce Structured Knowledge Injection (LLM+), a lightweight method that integrates structured knowledge into LLMs to enhance their reasoning capabilities. This approach involves two stages: first, a pre-trained LLM generates a knowledge graph from raw data, and second, a graph neural network (GNN) processes the graph to create embeddings that are injected into the LLM. We evaluated LLM+ on three distinct knowledge injection tasks: mathematical reasoning, question answering, and natural language inference. The results indicate that LLM+ significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, including T5-Base, T5-Large, BERT-Base, BERT-Large, RoBERTa-Base, RoBERTa-Large, and DeBERTa-v3-Base. Furthermore, the framework is flexible and can be applied to various NLP tasks. The code and data are available at https://github.com/Abhinav-1999/SKILL.

Non-linear non-extensive entropy is hypothesized to be the root cause of the anomalous specific heat observed in Anti-de Sitter (AdS) black holes. This paper examines the thermodynamic stability of non-extensive shaded AdS charged AdS black holes. Our findings indicate that non-extensivity amplifies thermodynamic instability, causing the stable shaded region to shrink as the non-extensive index increases. Furthermore, we observe that the first-order phase transition temperature rises with the non-extensive index, implying that non-extensive effects can prolong the duration of thermal equilibrium between small and large phases. Additionally, we demonstrate that the non-extensive index influences the first-order phase transition temperature, which in turn affects the stability of the large black hole phase. Finally, we establish that the non-extensive index impacts the critical temperature, thereby altering the stability of the small black hole phase. These results suggest that non-extensive effects are significant in the thermodynamics of AdS charged black holes. The analysis of the shaded thermodynamics of non-linear AdS charged AdS black holes offers valuable insights into the phase structure of such systems. Our results may also provide guidance for understanding the thermodynamic phase structure of non-extensive non-linear shaded AdS black holes. Ultimately, this study could contribute to a deeper comprehension of the thermal equilibrium phases of non-extensive non-linear shaded Reissner-Nordström black holes. The shaded thermodynamics of non-linear non-extensive AdS charged AdS black holes warrants further investigation.

Quantum entanglement and synchronization represent two distinct non-classical phenomena that can coexist in specific quantum states. This study examines the entanglement and synchronization characteristics of the Wigner-Weyl quantum tomograms for vacuum, thermal, and squeezed vacuum states of two harmonic oscillators. The analysis reveals that in thermal and vacuum states, entanglement disappears before synchronization emerges, whereas squeezed vacuum states exhibit the opposite sequence. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that both entanglement and synchronization manifest as non-affine deformations within the corresponding quantum tomograms. These findings offer valuable insights for future investigations into quantum non-classical phenomena. The research was conducted by the Department of Physics, Tezpur University, Tezpur 784036, Assam, India.

Using $2.8\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of $\Upsilon(5S)$ collision data, the search for the $B_s^0\to\bar{D}^0 K_S^0$ and $B_s^0\to\bar{D}^{*0} K_S^0$ decay modes is conducted via reconstruction of the $D^0\to K^+\pi^-$ and $D^{*0}\to D^0\gamma$ final states. The analysis employs a binned maximum likelihood fit to determine the signal yield, which is subsequently used to calculate the branching fractions. The measured branching fraction for $B_s^0\to\bar{D}^0 K_S^0$ is $(1.91\pm0.11(\mathrm{stat.})\pm0.09(\mathrm{syst.})\pm0.10(\mathrm{BR.}))\times10^{-2}$, in agreement with the theoretical prediction of $(1.92\pm0.10(\mathrm{theory.}))\times10^{-2}$. For the first time, evidence is observed for the $B_s^0\to\bar{D}^{*0} K_S^0$ decay mode, with a calculated branching fraction of $(0.84\pm0.17(\mathrm{stat.})\pm0.07(\mathrm{syst.})\pm0.07(\mathrm{BR.}))\times10^{-2}$. These results are derived from the product of the yield and the ratio of the detection efficiencies for the two decay channels. Additionally, the differential charge conjugate decay $B_s^0\to\bar{D}^0 K_S^0$ is identified for the first time.

This paper presents an algorithm to construct the complete diagram of $M$'s submodules, where $M$ is a multiplicity-free module over a classical Lie algebra, utilizing only a subset of its multiplicities and the corresponding partial submodule lattice. The approach involves creating a potential lattice from the available partial information and refining it through a series of iterations. We demonstrate this algorithm by generating the lattice of submodules for several well-known modules. Additionally, we establish that the collection of all maximal proper submodules of $M$ forms a chain if and only if $M$ is a highest weight module. Furthermore, we derive the exact multiplicity of the zero weight and identify the unique maximal proper submodule that contains all other maximal proper submodules. Finally, we introduce a method to decompose $M$ into a direct sum of two proper submodules. The algorithms described in this work are implemented in Maple and accessible via the GitHub repository: https://github.com/ahmedshoukr/SubmoduleLattice.

This paper examines biharmonic hypersurfaces equipped with recurrent or semi-recurrent mechanisms within Euclidean space. It is demonstrated that a biharmonic hypersurface in Euclidean space, possessing a recurrent or semi-recurrent shape operator, must be an extrinsic product of a space form and a Euclidean space. Furthermore, it is proven that a biharmonic hypersurface in Euclidean space with a recurrent or semi-recurrent mean curvature vector, whose ambient dimension exceeds three, cannot exist. These findings extend and generalize earlier results documented in the literature.

A subset $A$ of the non-negative integers is termed $p/q$-recognizable if the formal power series associated with $A$ is rational and possesses poles exclusively at points of the form $\zeta (\sqrt[q]{p})^k$, where $\zeta$ is a root of unity. This concept was initially explored by Berstel, Perrin, and Reutenauer under the name $p/q$-regular. The set of non-negative integers satisfying this property is referred to as a $p/q$-identifiable set. While it is established that every finite set is $p/q$-identifiable, it was recently demonstrated by Krob and the current authors that no infinite arithmetic progression shares this characteristic. In this work, we introduce the notion of a $p/q$-recognizable language and prove that a language is $p/q$-recognizable if and only if it is regular and its characteristic sequence forms an ultimately periodic sequence that constitutes a $p/q$-identifiable set. Furthermore, we show that for any prime $p$ and integer $q \ge 2$, the set of primes constitutes a $p/q$-identifiable set. Finally, we provide a characterization of identifiable sets within the family of $k$-regular sequences.

When an adhesive tape is peeled, the sound emitted exhibits crackling noise characterized by intermittent stick-slip dynamics. This study investigates the acoustic signal generated by a Scotch tape pulled at a constant velocity. We observe that the noise spectrum displays a non-monotonic dependence on the pulling speed, featuring a distinct peak. Furthermore, the acoustic signal reveals self-affine characteristics, allowing for the definition of a Hurst exponent that serves as a measure of long-term memory. Our analysis indicates that the Hurst exponent and the noise spectrum peak are interconnected. These findings suggest that intermittent stick-slip events follow self-affine dynamics governed by a single scaling exponent. Consequently, the emergence of 1/f noise corresponds to a specific value of this Hurst exponent. These results align with those obtained from frictional sliding between solid blocks and offer insights into the stick-slip dynamics of an adhesive tape. Such dynamics are also relevant to the frictional sliding of geological faults, which can trigger seismic events. The experimental setup is illustrated in Figure 1, where an adhesive tape is peeled from a surface while the resulting acoustic signal is recorded.

In 1928, during the creation of his book *Geometries*, Menger posed two questions regarding the embeddability of angle spaces into metric spaces. For nearly a century, these inquiries remained unresolved, with existing attempts ultimately failing. This paper offers solutions to both problems by demonstrating that the standard definition of the angle function in a space $X$ is insufficient for ensuring the embeddability of $X$ into a metric space. We introduce a novel function, $\widehat{\angle}$, which serves as a natural extension of the angle function and fulfills additional requirements necessary for embeddability. By utilizing $\widehat{\angle}$, we define a new structure, the $\widehat{\angle}$-space, and prove that an angle space $X$ can be embedded into a metric space if and only if its associated $\widehat{\angle}$-space satisfies this condition. Consequently, we establish that Euclidean and Hilbert spaces are $\widehat{\angle}$-spaces, and we show that $L_1$-spaces and certain other metric spaces do not possess this property. Furthermore, we confirm that for any dimension $n\geq 2$, the space of rational points within Euclidean $n$-space can be embedded into a specific $n$-dimensional metric space that is not an $L_1$-space. Finally, we provide a complete characterization of embeddable $\widehat{\angle}$-spaces into metric spaces and into Euclidean spaces. These results yield a positive solution to a longstanding open problem concerning the embeddability of Euclidean spaces of dimension at least three into $L_1$-spaces. Our findings also have significant implications for the study of Euclidean spaces and related structures, such as spherical and hyperbolic spaces. In this context, the function $\widehat{\angle}$ acts as a natural substitute for the traditional angle function, and the concept of a $\widehat{\angle}$-space serves as a valuable substitute for that of an angle space.

Neural network models have achieved significant success in processing point cloud data, yet their deployment in safety-critical domains like autonomous driving remains hindered by a lack of robustness against adversarial attacks. These attacks exploit the deterministic nature of point cloud representations to deceive models. This paper introduces TPC, a transformation-unique smoothing technique designed to enhance the robustness of point cloud models. Unlike conventional smoothing methods that rely on stochastic sampling, TPC generates a unique representation for each input point cloud by applying a series of transformations. We demonstrate that a carefully selected sequence of transformations can yield a uniform distribution over the input's feature space. Furthermore, we prove that this approach offers stronger robustness guarantees than traditional sampling-based smoothing. Extensive experiments show that TPC significantly improves the robustness of various point cloud models against diverse adversarial attack strategies. The source code is available at https://github.com/tpc-smoothing/TPC-Point-Cloud-Smoothing.

Testing remains the most extensively utilized technique for enhancing software quality, yet it is frequently constrained by the difficulty of creating effective test cases. This paper introduces a geometric framework designed to automate the selection of high-quality test cases for a specific program. The proposed method integrates symbolic execution with a geometric algorithm to identify test inputs that maximize code coverage. By employing a simple random walk algorithm within a geometric space, the approach generates inputs aimed at increasing coverage. We implemented this technique in a tool called GeoTest and evaluated it against state-of-the-art solutions using the Big-Benchmark and CMU Terse benchmarks. The results demonstrate that GeoTest achieves superior code coverage compared to existing methods. Furthermore, the implementation of GeoTest is accessible at https://github.com/GeoTest/GeoTest.

This paper offers a concise proof of the existence of $\ell$-adic Serre weights for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ corresponding to irreducible diagonalizable characteristic zero representations of the local Galois group, utilizing Kummer theory. Additionally, we establish that these weights are unique when the local Galois representation is cyclic. As a byproduct, we provide a streamlined demonstration of the local existence of potentially diagonalizable crystalline lifts of irreducible representations, which had originally been shown by Paškūnas. Finally, we derive a simplified proof of the local existence of potentially Barshtype lifts of irreducible representations, first demonstrated by Herzig.

Fiber-reinforced composites integrating carbon nanofibers (CNF) and shape memory polymer (SMP) phases represent a promising active damage control strategy. These materials offer self-sensing and self-actuating capabilities, enabling real-time monitoring and mitigation of damage. This study introduces a novel damage shaping technique for self-sensing composites via electrical impedance tomography (EIT) to optimize the reconstruction of damage geometry. Concurrently, a genetic algorithm (GA) was employed to determine the optimal damage geometry required to return a damaged composite to its original configuration. The results indicate that the GA successfully identified the ideal geometry for repairing a 12.7 mm crack in a [0/90]s laminate, reducing the tip opening displacement by 91.1% and restoring the global stiffness to 98.4% of its initial state. Furthermore, the reconstructed images from the electrical impedance tomography (EIT) align closely with the geometry predicted by the genetic algorithm, confirming the efficacy of the proposed damage shaping approach.

This work introduces a novel geometric tensor framework for Euclidean spaces, grounded in the concept of oriented areas. We define a rank-2 tensor, termed the area tensor, associated with each pair of vectors. This tensor enables the definition of an oriented area scalar for any two vectors. We demonstrate that fundamental Euclidean geometric scalars—including lengths, angles, scalar products, vector products, and triple products—can be expressed through the area scalar and the area tensor. Furthermore, we establish that all standard Euclidean geometric scalars, as well as the scalar product and contraction operations, remain invariant under transformations of the area tensor. Leveraging these invariants, we derive a generalized Pythagorean theorem applicable to any set of vectors. Finally, we derive a generalized Gram determinant that relies solely on the area tensor and the area scalar. As an application, we derive explicit expressions for the Riemann curvature tensor and the Ricci tensor using only the area tensor and area scalar. We conclude by deriving the Frenet-Serret formulas for curves and hypersurfaces within Euclidean spaces, based entirely on the area tensor and area scalar. The proposed framework offers a fresh perspective on Euclidean geometry, potentially aiding in the development of a corresponding geometry for Minkowski spaces. Such an approach could be valuable for special and general relativity, as well as for theoretical physics in general. Additionally, this framework may benefit computer science, particularly in areas involving 3D graphics and robotics. The underlying concept of an "area tensor" for pairs of vectors could find applications in various fields, including physics, mathematics, and computer science. For instance, in physics, it could be useful for analyzing the geometry of particle collisions, where the colliding particles correspond to specific pairs of vectors. In mathematics, it could support the study of Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometries. In computer science, it could enhance 3D graphics, robotics, and related technologies. Ultimately, this framework provides a new language for describing Euclidean geometry, potentially offering benefits across multiple disciplines. Readers interested in the historical development of geometric algebra and its connection to this approach are directed to the references cited in this paper. Those wishing to explore the application of the area tensor to Minkowski spaces should consult the related work by the same authors on that topic.

This paper examines splittings of the commutative diagram of groups associated with a graph monomial poset for a right-angled Artin group. We demonstrate that if the corresponding right-angled Artin complex admits a non-trivial (n+1)-splitting, then the graph monomial poset must possess a non-trivial rank 2 splitting. Leveraging this result, we construct a collection of counterexamples to the commutative diagram conjecture for right-angled Artin groups. Furthermore, we establish that for a specific class of right-angled Artin groups, the conjecture holds true. As a byproduct, we provide a characterization of when the commutative diagram conjecture is valid for star graphs. Additionally, we prove that for a particular family of right-angled Artin complexes, any non-trivial splitting arises from a folding. These findings extend a result by Bestvina, Feighn, and Handel regarding splittings of hyperbolic groups. Finally, we show that for a certain class of right-angled Artin complexes, every non-trivial splitting is a graph of complexes where all vertex and edge stabilizers are themselves complexes.

This paper introduces a novel iterative algorithm for inverting large, sparse, positive definite matrices, potentially yielding significant speedups over conventional methods. The approach generalizes a high-order technique originally designed for low-rank updates to a broader class of matrices. We provide a detailed description of the algorithm, prove its convergence, and establish an $O(n^2/h)$ complexity per iteration, where $n$ represents the matrix dimension and $h$ is a parameter influencing both convergence rate and complexity. Extensive numerical experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the method's practical advantages. The implementation, titled HOSI (Higher Order Inversion), is available at https://github.com/rohitgupta1996/HOSI. Compared to standard Cholesky decomposition, our method achieves substantial acceleration for matrices with $n > 10^5$, and for smaller matrices, performance gains are observed when the sparsity exceeds 99.9%. Furthermore, for matrices with $n > 10^6$, the algorithm delivers significant improvements over state-of-the-art iterative approaches. These results indicate that Higher Order Inversion is a viable solution for inverting extremely large, sparse, positive definite matrices. The implementation has been tested on matrices with up to $10^9$ elements and is adaptable to various matrix types, including non-sparse ones. For such cases, the complexity per iteration can be further reduced by approximating the inverse of the low-rank update term using low-rank matrix multiplication. This adaptation offers a promising direction for future research. Additionally, the implementation supports GPU acceleration, which can further enhance performance. For instance, inverting a $10^6 \times 10^6$ matrix with 99.9% sparsity took 10 minutes on a single GPU, whereas the same task required 1.5 hours on a CPU. The implementation also accommodates complex matrices. Finally, the algorithm can be integrated into existing inversion methods, such as Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury based approaches, to achieve additional speedups. For example, combining Higher Order Inversion with the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury method reduced the runtime for inverting a $10^7 \times 10^7$ matrix with 99.9% sparsity from 10 hours to 1.5 hours on a single GPU. These results suggest that Higher Order Inversion is a valuable technique for accelerating large-scale matrix inversions in applications like MIMO

Contextual linear bandits represent a foundational model for personalized decision-making in applications like recommender systems, where an agent selects actions based on observed contexts to maximize cumulative rewards. In a federated setup, the objective is to achieve near-optimal performance without requiring data to leave local sites or necessitating access to the raw datasets of other participants. Existing federated approaches for contextual linear bandits typically rely on two-stage methods that utilize explicit or implicit linear regression to estimate action-value functions. However, these regression-based techniques are ill-suited for distributed contextual linear bandit problems, where contexts are non-i.i.d. and potentially sparse, as they often fail to deliver optimal results. This work introduces a novel learning algorithm for distributed contextual linear bandits that operates without any form of data sharing or reliance on linear models. The proposed method achieves a nearly optimal cumulative regret of $O(d\sqrt{T\log T})$, where $T$ represents the time horizon and $d$ is the dimensionality of the context vector. Furthermore, the algorithm is easily implementable in real-world scenarios and does not require pre-processing of historical data. Extensive simulations demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in federated contextual linear bandit settings. The source code is available at https://github.com/Abhishek-1999/DiLeCoLeB.

We re-examine the vertical shear instability (VSI) in the outer regions of protoplanetary disks, incorporating dust evolution into our model. Our findings indicate that dust settling and radial drift significantly suppress VSI-driven turbulence, reducing the viscous timescale by up to two orders of magnitude. This suppression occurs because dust evolution mitigates vertical temperature gradients, which are the primary driver of the VSI. Furthermore, we observe that the VSI's suppression by dust evolution is more pronounced in the inner regions of the disk, where gas temperatures are higher and the instability is more sensitive to thermal gradients. These results suggest that VSI-driven turbulence is unlikely to account for the high accretion rates observed in outer regions where dust evolution is active. Consequently, other mechanisms must be responsible for sustaining high accretion rates in these areas. Additionally, our results imply that gas and dust may decouple in the outer regions of protoplanetary disks, potentially altering the growth rates of dust instabilities such as the streaming and gravitational instabilities. Finally, we conclude that dust evolution could extend the growth timescale of planetestons formed via dust instabilities in the outer regions, potentially explaining the absence of such bodies in those zones. Our study underscores the critical role of dust evolution in regulating accretion and dust instabilities in protoplanetary disks. The source code for this work is accessible at https://github.com/Aniruddha-1999/Dust_VSI.

This study examines Liouville-type theorems for harmonic functions and shrinkers defined on gradient shrinking Ricci solitons that possess uniform scalar curvature. As a primary outcome, a gradient estimate for harmonic functions under the specified conditions is established. Furthermore, the concept of $\mathcal{R}$-bounded geometry is introduced, and it is demonstrated that if the manifold $M$ satisfies $|Rm| \leq C$ and $|
abla Rm| \leq \epsilon$, then $M$ exhibits $\mathcal{R}$-bounded geometry. Leveraging this concept, the notion of $\mathcal{R}$-harmonic functions is defined, and a Liouville theorem regarding $\mathcal{R}$-harmonic functions is proven. Finally, as a significant consequence, the concept of Ricci-bounded solitons is introduced, and it is shown that any complete steady soliton with $|Rm| \leq C$ and $|
abla Rm| \leq \epsilon$ must be a gradient shrinking soliton. Additionally, the existence of a complete steady soliton with $|Rm| \leq C$ and $|
abla Rm| \leq \epsilon$ on a non-shrinking soliton is ruled out. These findings extend the work of Cabezas-Raines and Lee (2012) and Perelman (2002). The concept of $\mathcal{R}$-bounded geometry and the associated Liouville theorem may find applications in proving no-collapse Ricci flow with $|Rm| \leq C$ and $|
abla Rm| \leq \epsilon$ on two- and three-dimensional manifolds.

Backdoor attacks represent a significant security risk in deep learning, where a model functions correctly for clean inputs but executes malicious actions when specific trigger patterns are present. While prior research has primarily focused on static triggers, this work introduces dynamic backdoors, which rely on input characteristics rather than fixed patterns to activate. We demonstrate that existing defenses against static backdoors, such as adversarial training, are ineffective against our dynamic variant. Furthermore, we show that neural network architectures utilizing global mean pooling (GMP)—a common layer in computer vision models—are particularly susceptible to these attacks. Extensive experiments across multiple image classification tasks confirm that our dynamic backdoor can achieve activation rates of 99.9%, surpassing the best results from current static backdoor methods. Additionally, we provide a detailed analysis of the attack's characteristics and its relationship with GMP. To our knowledge, this is the first study to examine dynamic backdoors and their connection to global pooling layers. The source code is available at https://github.com/Abhishek-1999/DB_with_GMP.

Federated learning represents a promising strategy for training machine learning models across geographically dispersed data sources without requiring data centralization. This approach is particularly valuable for handling heterogeneous data, where different data sources possess varying feature spaces. However, existing methods often fail to scale effectively when dealing with highly diverse datasets. In this work, we introduce a random walk-based algorithm designed to address heterogeneous data within a federated learning framework. Our algorithm enables a data source to learn a model from its local data and simultaneously collect predictions generated by other sources' models, thereby indirectly gaining exposure to their feature spaces. Through iterative cycles of local learning and prediction gathering, the algorithm constructs a global model that leverages both direct and indirect data experiences. We theoretically demonstrate that, under specific conditions, the global model can achieve performance comparable to a fully supervised global model trained on all data. Extensive experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets confirm that our algorithm outperforms current approaches for heterogeneous data, including embedding-based methods. These results validate the effectiveness of our random walk-based algorithm in learning from highly diverse data sources. Ultimately, this method offers a viable solution for training global models on truly heterogeneous datasets, a challenge that has remained unresolved until now. Our approach is simple, scalable, and requires no assumptions regarding the underlying data distribution. Furthermore, it operates without the need for a central server, making it ideal for privacy-sensitive applications. The proposed algorithm is open-source and available at: https://github.com/Abhishek-1999/StrollForLearning.

Consistency regularization remains a dominant approach for semi-supervised medical image segmentation, relying on the prediction of an auxiliary network for unlabeled data. However, this method often struggles with overfitting on the limited labeled dataset, which degrades segmentation quality. In this paper, we introduce a novel consistency regularization technique that directly leverages the segmentation outputs of the auxiliary network rather than its predictions. We demonstrate that this shift in focus yields significant performance gains. Furthermore, we propose a simple yet effective strategy to mitigate the risk of the auxiliary network generating nonsensical segmentation results. Extensive experiments across three medical image datasets confirm that our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art methods. The source code is available at: https://github.com/ChenYan0909/ACS.

Genuine nonlocal effects, such as Bell nonlocality and nonlocal correlations, are typically observed in multipartite systems where entanglement exists between distinct parties. In contrast, single-particle entanglement has historically been viewed merely as a resource for tasks like remote state preparation, steering, and nonlocal correlations, without manifesting as a genuine nonlocal phenomenon. This perspective shifts with our demonstration that single-particle entanglement can produce genuine nonlocal effects, including single-particle Bell nonlocality and single-particle nonlocality within steering scenarios. We establish that the previously identified single-particle nonlocality in steering scenarios represents only a specific instance of a broader phenomenon: genuine single-particle Bell nonlocality. Furthermore, we show that this effect can be amplified by increasing the dimensionality of the entanglement. Crucially, we prove that genuine single-particle nonlocality enables the violation of a Bell inequality through a scenario involving three spatially separated locations and two parties, where one party performs measurements on a single entangled particle. This result confirms that a genuine nonlocal effect can occur across a tripartite system—even when only two parties are present—despite the particle visiting just two of the three locations. Consequently, we conclude that single-particle entanglement gives rise to a genuine nonlocal phenomenon, which we term "single-particle nonlocality." This phenomenon is analogous to how multipartite entanglement leads to multipartite nonlocality, such as standard Bell nonlocality. Ultimately, we argue that single-particle nonlocality should be regarded as the genuine nonlocal manifestation of single-particle entanglement, mirroring the relationship between multipartite nonlocality and multipartite entanglement.

Federated learning (FL) represents a promising approach for training machine learning models across distributed systems without exchanging raw data, thereby enhancing data privacy. Concurrently, blockchain technology offers robust security and privacy mechanisms through its decentralized architecture, immutability, and transparency. Although both technologies have been extensively investigated individually, their combined application remains underexplored. This study provides a comprehensive survey on integrating blockchain with FL frameworks specifically designed for Internet of Vehicles (IoV) systems. We examine the potential benefits, challenges, and open issues associated with this integration, ultimately proposing future research directions. The survey is structured into three sections: an overview of IoV, FL, and blockchain technologies; a detailed analysis of blockchain-enabled FL frameworks for IoV; and a discussion of advantages, limitations, and potential future research areas. By offering a thorough survey of blockchain-empowered FL frameworks for IoV, this work aims to guide researchers in developing secure, privacy-preserving, and efficient learning systems for intelligent IoV environments. The corresponding taxonomy is illustrated in Figure 1. This survey is organized as follows: Section 2 introduces foundational concepts of IoV, FL, and blockchain; Section 3 reviews blockchain-empowered FL frameworks for IoV; Section 4 discusses the benefits, challenges, and future research directions; and Section 5 concludes the paper.

Long short-term memory (LSTM) networks are a deep learning architecture widely adopted for sequence modeling tasks, such as video identification. Despite their success, LSTMs are computationally intensive and characterized by high memory usage, which hinders their deployment on resource-constrained hardware. This paper introduces an algorithm and hardware co-design framework aimed at optimizing the energy efficiency of LSTMs for video identification. Our approach begins with a hardware-oriented LSTM decomposition that balances energy efficiency against accuracy. Subsequently, we apply Tucker tensor decomposition to the weight matrices resulting from the LSTM decomposition to further enhance energy efficiency. To address the increased memory footprint caused by Tucker decomposition, we propose a low-overhead hardware design for matrix multiplication that utilizes a time-multiplexed strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that our co-design framework achieves significant energy efficiency gains. Specifically, when processing 720p videos, the LSTM-decomposed and tensor-decomposed network (LTD-TD) delivers a 1.75× improvement in energy efficiency compared to the original LSTM, and a 1.5× improvement over the state-of-the-art hierarchical Tucker decomposition (HTD). Furthermore, the LTD-TD architecture offers superior energy efficiency across various video resolutions and compression ratios. Finally, we trained the LTD-TD network on the TRECVID 2019 dataset and achieved a top-5 identification accuracy of 54.0%, surpassing the accuracy of the HTD model on the same dataset. The source code for this work is available at: https://github.com/zhengyong99/LSTM_Tensor_Decomposition.

This paper presents a novel characterization of prime numbers, which serves as a computationally efficient method for identifying primes. We also examine the computationally intensive nature of the characterization's components. Furthermore, we apply this characterization to the iteration of the composition of polynomial functions. The results indicate that, aside from the constant polynomials $f(x)=x$ and $f(x)=x+1$, no polynomial of degree $n\geq 2$ can be expressed as the $k$-th iteration of the composition of a polynomial of degree $m\geq 2$, where $k\geq 2$. Additionally, we demonstrate that this characterization can be utilized to derive other significant results regarding the iteration of polynomial compositions. Finally, we conclude by discussing potential future research directions. The proposed characterization of prime numbers may also find applications in other areas of mathematics.

This study examines the Schr\"odinger equation on the region outside a convex obstacle, subject to nonlinear boundary conditions. We demonstrate that the solution blows up in finite time for initial data with negative energy, provided the initial wavefunction is sufficiently concentrated. Conversely, we establish global existence for initial data with non-negative energy. These findings extend earlier work by the authors, which considered boundary conditions of power type, to a broader class of nonlinearities. Additionally, we derive new results regarding the monotonicity of the mass and energy functionals. The analysis relies on the concavity method and a refined version of Strichartz estimates adapted to the Schr\"odinger equation with nonlinear boundary conditions.

This work introduces a semi-parametric adaptation of the local extension by variables technique, originally developed by Huneke, Katz, and Valdes-Gonzalez in 2019. Utilizing this approach, we demonstrate that if a variety defined over a finitely generated $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra admits a local uniform reduction in characteristic zero, then a positive-characteristic counterpart exists. As a direct consequence, we establish that for a variety $X$ over a finitely generated $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra $A$, the condition of being set-theoretically complete-intersection in all positive characteristics is both necessary and sufficient for a local uniform reduction in characteristic zero to exist. Furthermore, we provide a characterization of varieties that are set-theoretically complete-intersection across all characteristics, including a proof of Theorem A. Finally, we show that a variety $X$ over $A$ possesses a local uniform reduction in characteristic zero if and only if it admits a local complete-intersection ideal $J$ such that $X=\mathbf{V}(J)$ and $J$ remains $\mu$-generated modulo the prime ideal $P$ corresponding to $X$ in $A/P$ for some integer $\mu$. These results generalize Theorem 1.1 from the paper by Choudhury, De Stefani, Herzog, and Vasconcellos titled: Set-theoretic complete intersections in all characteristics, Journal of Algebra 552 (2020), 213--231. Bayes factors serve as a primary metric for model comparison in Bayesian statistics, offering a theoretically ideal solution for selecting among competing models. However, their practical application has been limited by concerns regarding robustness. This paper reviews recent literature addressing these issues and introduces a novel approach to enhance the robustness of Bayes factors. We evaluate various strategies for utilizing Bayes factors to guide model selection, with a specific focus on a new method that integrates model averaging. Through an extensive analysis of a real-world dataset involving the detection of gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers, we compare these different approaches. Our results indicate that, for this specific dataset, the choice of workflow does not significantly alter the final model selection outcome. Furthermore, we demonstrate how to apply these strategies to a range of realistic datasets characterized by high dimensionality and complexity. Ultimately, we advocate for the adoption of robustness testing as a standard procedure when employing Bayes factors for model selection. The source code for all methods discussed in this work is accessible at https://github.com/robertgrosset/WorkflowStrategiesForBayesFactors.

Discourse markers (DMs) are lexical items that signal relationships between clauses, sentences, or larger textual segments. While numerous studies have attempted to classify DMs based on the relationships they express, these efforts have predominantly relied on manual annotation by linguists. This approach is both labor-intensive and prone to subjectivity. In this work, we introduce a fully automatic method for creating a taxonomy of DMs within the English Wikipedia, grounded in the semantic analysis of hypernyms found in structured abstracts of discourse marker articles. We evaluate the taxonomy's quality using human-annotated datasets and an existing automatic classifier trained on those datasets. Furthermore, we apply the taxonomy to a collection of errors from the Meta-Data Quality Campaign (MDQC) to identify potential misclassifications of DMs in Wikipedia article titles. Our results indicate that the proposed taxonomy aligns well with existing taxonomies, as evidenced by strong agreement with human annotations on test datasets and high performance on an existing automatic evaluation dataset. Additionally, our analysis of MDQC errors reveals that a significant number of potential title misclassifications for DMs in the English Wikipedia stem from errors in the article's structured abstract rather than the use of the marker itself. To support this examination, we have made our dataset, taxonomy, and analytical tools available at https://github.com/linguamatics/DiscSense.

This paper introduces a family of Jordanian twists derived from the universal $R$-matrix of the negative Borel subalgebra of the quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. These twists are constructed by extending the standard Jordanian twist, which originates from the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, utilizing the explicit formulation of the universal $R$-matrix provided by Faddeev, Reshetikhin, and Takhtajan. It is demonstrated that this family of Jordanian twists yields deformations of the tensor product of regular representations of the corresponding Lie bialgebra of $sl_2$. Furthermore, the modified universal $R$-matrix resulting from the double of the negative Borel subalgebra of the deformed quantum group is explicitly calculated. The study concludes by examining the potential applications of these Jordanian twists in the context of noncommutative geometry.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm for determining the validity of existential regular expression (RE) constraints over an extended RE syntax that incorporates complementation. This syntax aligns with a recently proposed formalism known as deterministic extended regular expressions (DeRE), which possesses a unique normal form. The algorithm operates by transforming the extended RE syntax into this normal form and subsequently solving the resulting constraints symbolically within the normal form domain. To demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy, we integrated it into the CREX tool and applied it to a collection of RE constraints extracted from literature. The results indicate that our algorithm can resolve constraints that were previously unsolvable by existing methods. Furthermore, we established the soundness and completeness of the algorithm and analyzed its time and space complexity. As an application, we utilized the algorithm to address open problems concerning the equivalence of DeREs and other regular expression syntaxes. The source code and additional details are accessible at https://github.com/crex-tool/solving-derex-constraints.

This study examines the commutator of OPE blocks constructed from primary fields in CFT$_{2}$, which correspond to the bulk geodesic Witten diagram in AdS$_{3}$. We demonstrate that the commutator of two geodesic OPE blocks decomposes into a sum of products involving spinning holomorphic and anti-holomorphic OPE blocks. By utilizing the decomposition of geodesic bulk-to-boundary propagations into spinning bulk-to-boundary propagations, we derive the explicit form of the commutator of two geodesic Witten diagrams expressed as a product of spinning OPE blocks. Consequently, we establish the decomposition of the product of two geodesic bulk-to-boundary propagations into a product of spinning bulk-to-boundary propagations. Furthermore, we verify the decomposition of the commutator of two geodesic Witten diagrams into a sum of products of spinning OPE blocks for the case of two identical bulk fields. Finally, we confirm the decomposition of the commutator of two bulk-to-bulk propagations into a product of spinning OPE blocks for the scenario involving two bulk fields and two boundary points. These results are significant for constructing higher-point Witten diagrams from OPE blocks and for analyzing the commutator of bulk-to-bulk propagations in AdS$_{3}$.

We introduce a novel architecture for lobster-eye X-ray optics, composed of multiple segmented sections that collectively cover extensive fields of view. This configuration enables the construction of telescopes with enhanced effective areas and broader fields of view than previously feasible. We present a theoretical framework for optimizing the layout of these segmented modules to maximize both effective area and field of view. Furthermore, we detail the design of a telescope capable of monitoring a 100,000 square degree field with an angular resolution of approximately 10 arcminutes across a 2-10 keV energy range. This instrument would be particularly valuable for observing X-ray transients and tracking variable sources. The multiplexed lobster-eye design offers a cost-effective solution for wide-field X-ray monitoring, potentially serving as a complementary system to current and future narrow-field observatories. We also discuss the potential for integrating this architecture with existing optics to create instruments with ultra-wide fields of view. Finally, we outline the design of a multiplexed lobster-eye telescope intended for deployment at the IXPE science operations center to monitor variable sources during imaging observations. This initiative is a collaborative effort involving the IXPE science operations team, the AST3 (Astrophysics X-ray Telemetry) project, and the RXT (Rapid X-ray Transient) project.

We introduce a novel approach to investigate the impact of the cosmic speed field (CSF) on the dark matter halo mass function (HMFn). By training a deep learning model on simulation data, we successfully reconstructed the HMFn across a range of halo masses ($10^{10} < M/M_{\odot} < 10^{15}$) and cosmic times ($0.005 < z < 2.0$) using only the power spectrum of the CSF as input. Our findings indicate that the HMFn is not solely determined by the power spectrum of density fluctuations, as traditionally assumed, but is also influenced by the power spectrum of velocity fluctuations. Furthermore, we observed that the reconstructed halo mass distribution shifts toward lower masses as the amplitude of velocity fluctuations increases. These results suggest that the CSF plays a significant role in determining the dark matter halo mass function. This study offers fresh insights into the formation of dark matter halos and their associated mass distribution. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/Anushka-1999/Unraveling_CSF_HMFN.

We demonstrate that an atomic interferometer can detect local magnetic field variations via the Meissner effect in a superconductor. This detection method is sensitive to local changes in the magnetic field vector, independent of the field's direction. Consequently, the atomic interferometer functions as a local vector magnetometer. In a local region, the superconductor acts as a magnetic flux tube, guiding the atomic wavefunction along a specific trajectory. This guidance creates an interference pattern that reveals local magnetic field variations. Our experiment achieved a sensitivity of 0.02 nT over an integration time of 10 seconds within a local region measuring 1.5 cm in diameter. This sensitivity surpasses that of conventional atomic interferometers, which rely on Sagnac or Bloch oscillation effects. Furthermore, because the sensitivity of this local detection scales with integration time, it exceeds the sensitivity of global detection methods. These findings suggest that local detection through the Meissner effect is a promising approach for enhancing the sensitivity of atomic interferometers. Additionally, this technique offers a simple means to detect local magnetic field variations in the local region of any atomic interferometer. Such detection could enable the measurement of gravitational wave-induced variations in local magnetic fields, potentially improving the sensitivity of gravitational wave detectors. Our demonstration confirms that the Meissner effect can be utilized to detect local magnetic field variations in atomic interferometry, potentially serving as a valuable tool for future gravitational wave detection. We present a relativistic first principles theory designed to investigate the spin structure and electronic characteristics of magnetic impurities and adatoms situated on superconducting surfaces. Utilizing the BSE@DFT framework, we examine the Yu--Shiba--Rusinov (YSR) states associated with an Mn adatom and various Mn clusters on the Nb(110) superconducting surface. Our analysis reveals that the YSR states for the Mn adatom and clusters are inherently relativistic in nature. Furthermore, the spin configuration of the YSR states is found to be sensitive to the specific Mn cluster geometry. These results indicate that the BSE@DFT approach offers valuable insights into the spin and electronic properties of adatoms and clusters on superconducting surfaces. The BSE@DFT framework is anticipated to be a valuable tool for exploring the spin structure of impurities and adatoms on superconductors, as well as for investigating superconductivity in materials containing magnetic impurities. This study introduces a novel framework for classifying skin cancer images, leveraging the strengths of both convolutional neural networks (CNN) and entropy. The proposed architecture consists of two parallel branches: the first employs a CNN to extract features from input images, while the second utilizes an entropy layer to transform these features into a scalar value. These scalar outputs are then fed into a fully connected layer, which generates the final classification. The framework was evaluated using the ISIC 2018 dataset, which contains 12,990 images across six categories: benign lesion, melanoma, melanocytic nevus, melanoma in situ, ulcer, and vascular lesion. Results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches on this dataset, achieving an accuracy of 99.01%, a precision of 99.01%, a recall of 99.01%, and an F1 score of 99.01%. Furthermore, the model demonstrated strong generalization capabilities when tested on the ISIC 2017 dataset, surpassing other methods in terms of AUC, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/AbdulrahmanAlshammari/SkinCancerClassification.

At forward angles, the exchange of virtual vector bosons between muons becomes a significant effect that can degrade the center-of-mass energy available for hard scattering. This phenomenon, known as electroweak Sudakov suppression, is particularly pronounced at high energies. To address this, we introduce an efficient implementation of the $W$-$Z$-gluon-parton (WGZ) framework within the fast-millennium (F*X) generator. This approach offers a computationally efficient alternative to the conventional matrix-element $\times$-parton-function (ME$\times$PF) method for calculating electroweak Sudakov corrections in muon collisions. By combining the ME$\times$PF and WGZ frameworks, we develop a unified model that accounts for both electroweak Sudakov suppression and the onset of weak boson-parton ($V$-parton) dynamics. Our analysis demonstrates that the WGZ framework yields superior results at extreme $x$ values, whereas the ME$\times$PF approach is more accurate at lower $x$. Furthermore, the two methods agree closely in the intermediate $x$ region. We also observe that the WGZ framework provides a more reliable description of $W$ and $Z$ boson production at high invariant mass. Finally, we find that the ME$\times$PF approach tends to overestimate the cross-section for muon pair production at central rapidities when the mass exceeds 2.5 TeV, an issue resolved by incorporating the WGZ framework. These results indicate that the efficient WGZ framework is essential for accurately modeling muon collision processes involving high-mass electroweak bosons and forward jets. To facilitate future research, we have made both the traditional ME$\times$PF and the new efficient WGZ frameworks publicly available as independent modules within the MuF-FX generator. These modules can be integrated into other Monte Carlo event generators, such as Pythia8, Herwig, Sherpa, and MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, to simulate parton-level processes with greater precision. The MuF-FX generator, which combines the traditional and efficient frameworks for muon pair production ($\mu^+\mu^-\to\mu^+\mu^-$) and a range of other processes, is also now publicly accessible. Invariant manifolds, such as fixed points and periodic orbits, represent fundamental structures within dynamical systems. This study examines invariant surfaces within three-dimensional fractional order systems. We demonstrate that invariant surfaces corresponding to fixed points and periodic orbits do not exist when the sum of the system's eigenvalues exceeds a specific threshold. Furthermore, we establish that invariant surfaces linked to homoclinic orbits are impossible if the system possesses a saddle-focus fixed point with eigenvalues satisfying particular conditions. These findings offer novel insights into the dynamics of three-dimensional fractional order systems. Notably, our results indicate that the complex behaviors associated with homoclinic bifurcations and chaos cannot occur in certain three-dimensional fractional order systems, a phenomenon that contrasts with the behaviors observed in their integer order counterparts.

This study addresses the inverse problem of reconstructing a complex boundary condition from interior acoustic measurements, specifically for a simply supported square plate interacting with an enclosed acoustic cavity. The boundary condition is modeled as a linear superposition of rigid, acoustic, and active components, with the extent of the active region remaining unknown. Reconstruction relies on minimizing the difference between interior acoustic field measurements and those predicted by a boundary element method (BEM) finite element method (FEM) coupled FEM/BEM model. The optimization employs a genetic algorithm to determine the size of the active boundary segment and a gradient-based algorithm to refine the associated boundary impedance. Validation using a measured modal response confirms that the reconstructed active boundary segment aligns closely with the actual setup. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the size of the active segment can be accurately recovered even when the initial guess for the genetic algorithm is significantly distant from the true value.

We introduce the simplest scoto-seesaw model featuring a minimal dark sector, which comprises a single scalar singlet and a scalar triplet. This framework offers a unified solution to the neutrino mass and dark matter (DM) puzzles through the extended seesaw and WIMP mechanisms. We conduct a comprehensive phenomenological analysis, detailing the parameter space required for correct neutrino oscillation data, stable DM, and vacuum stability. Our study includes a thorough examination of direct DM detection prospects, collider signatures, and neutrinoless double beta decay. We find that achieving viable neutrino oscillation parameters and stable DM necessitates significant fine-tuning. Consequently, direct DM detection and specific collider signatures emerge as the most promising avenues for testing this model. To facilitate further research, we have made the model's Feynman rules, tree-level spectrum, and leading-order Feynman diagrams for all processes accessible via FeynAr3/DrawAr3 and MadGraph5_aMC@NLO. Additionally, we analyzed the impact of loop corrections on vacuum stability and DM stability, observing that these effects are negligible within the parameter regions satisfying all phenomenological constraints. Our findings indicate that, with the exception of neutrinoless double beta decay, all phenomenological constraints can be simultaneously satisfied. Notably, the scalar singlet and neutrino mass generation mechanisms remain robust against loop corrections, whereas the scalar triplet mass requires fine-tuning to ensure vacuum and DM stability. Finally, we determined that the direct detection signal strength is highly sensitive to the scalar triplet mass, particularly when the singlet and neutrino masses are fixed to their phenomenologically preferred values.
